subject: Pre-QBR: Launch stability forecasting and mitigation sync
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Elena Morris <elena@nimbushealth.com>, Nate Li <nate.li@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 12 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pre-QBR: Launch stability forecasting and mitigation sync

Team / Elena & Nate,

As we prep the QBR next week I want to surface the current stability forecast for the July product rollout and confirm a short remediation plan we can present. High-level summary first:

- On-path: core inference API for 1.0 feature set (text gen + embeddings) is green for scale tests up to 120 QPS with 95th latency within SLO.
- At-risk: two regressions we found in the last perf sweep (KV cache thrash on long-tail sessions, and a memory leak traced to our sharded batching coordinator) could affect peak-day tail latency.
- Impact window: these regressions are most likely to surface when sequence length > 2k combined with sustained concurrency > 80 QPS.

Ask: Can the core eng owners confirm current mitigation commitments and whether we can land the hotfix + extended soak by Friday EOD? If not, we should plan a conservative rollout and an exec-facing mitigation slide.

I attached the latest timeline and a distilled risk register (preview in email) for the QBR deck. Proposed next steps:
1) Monica: update risk register with severity + owner and confirm whether hotfix is on track.
2) Rishi: estimate rollback blast radius and a safe rollout cadence if we must throttle new customers on day-1.
3) Laura: advise on the executive framing — do we present a single-commitment plan or a bifurcated go/no-go scenario?

Elena / Nate: want to surface the dependency on your side too — if we need a conservative launch, what hard date ranges would break downstream commitments on your integrations?

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, PM (Product Platform)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: launch_timeline_v3.pdf, risk_register_v2.xlsx

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morris <elena@nimbushealth.com>, Nate Li <nate.li@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pre-QBR: Launch stability forecasting and mitigation sync

Thanks Karthik — I pulled the risk register into a focused sheet and attached v2. Quick notes from engineering triage: 

- Root cause & current status:
  * KV cache thrash: happens when clients open many short-lived sessions with large prefixes. Fix: guardrail added to batching coordinator and an LRU cache patch in QA branch. Initial soak runs show improvement but we need a 36-hour extended soak under production-like traces.
  * Memory leak: reproducible in internal stress harness via the sharded coordinator; fix is a patch to the allocator path. CI + perf regression tests pass on feature branch; deploying to canary now.

- Proposed mitigation timeline (compressed):
  1) Friday EOD: land memory-leak patch to canary (Rishi owns deploy).
  2) Saturday-Sunday: extended soak with production traces (Monica owns soak monitoring).
  3) Monday AM: if soak passes, roll to 25% with throttling knobs (Monica + Rishi).

- Failure modes and mitigations included in the register: fallback model variant, rolling restarts, customer-level throttles.

I marked severity: KV thrash = Medium-High, Memory leak = High (because of unbounded OOM risk). I've assigned owners in the attached sheet. If we can't validate soak by Monday, recommend we present the conservative rollout window for QBR and offer a clear remediation timeline.

I'll update the drive checklist (DOCS-PreQBR-Checklist) after the canary run.

--
Monica Patel
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: risk_register_v2.xlsx

From: Elena Morris <elena@nimbushealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jul 2028 16:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Pre-QBR: Launch stability forecasting and mitigation sync

Karthik / Monica,

Appreciate the transparency — we can adjust our integration cutover windows if you opt for a conservative rollout. Two notes from our side: 

- Our internal release calendar has a hard dependency on a July 24th cutover for several clinics. If you delay beyond July 25th it will cascade into our vendor timelines and require an exception approval.
- For a conservative rollout we need a documented API compatibility guarantee and a rollback path communicated 24 hrs before any customer migration.

If you think you can commit to the Monday AM 25% ramp (post-soak), we'll hold July 24th as target and proceed with our end. If not, we'll need a short call to renegotiate dates with our program office.

Regards,
Elena
Head of Integrations
Nimbus Health

On Fri, Jul 12, 2028 at 10:05 AM Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com> wrote:

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Elena Morris <elena@nimbushealth.com>, Nate Li <nate.li@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jul 2028 19:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pre-QBR: Launch stability forecasting and mitigation sync

Thanks all — good clarity. Two quick leadership-level notes for the QBR slide and the exec ask: 

1) Narrative: we will present a single primary plan with conditional pathing. Primary plan = proceed with canary + extended soak and targeted 25% ramp Monday if soak passes. Conditional path = defer full rollout and present the remediation timeline (48–72 hrs) with rollback options. Keep the language tight: Signal, Impact, Ask.

2) Ask for the QBR: we need a single-line commitment for each owner that I can put on the slide. Please reply to this email confirming your one-line: owner / commitment / worst-case delay. Example: "Monica / canary + 36-hr soak by Sat; worst-case +5 days to full ramp."

Monica, Rishi, Karthik — please reply with that one-line by EOD PST so I can finalize the QBR deck and the executive talking points. Elena — we will aim for Monday 25% ramp; I'll confirm Friday night after soak.

Laura Bennett
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: (none)
